prompt: Vertical 9:16 editorial advertising photograph, a full-bleed photograph edge to edge, with no borders, bands or panels: a close still life of two cupped hands at night, seen from slightly above. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. It confirms the open braid and the flat disc; ignore its plaster block too. Build it exactly: 2 round hoops, 25 mm across, each a 5-6 mm open plait: polished round wires laid in pairs, braided in chevrons over a see-through core of finer wires. 1 flat 8 mm disc at the top on the latch side, 1 thin hinged latch wire, 0 stones, no bottom loop. 18k gold tone, mirror polish. Must stay a many-wire open braid, never a smooth tube, simple twist or oval. Exactly one flat disc on each hoop, never two and never none; the disc, the hinge, the latch wire and every wire of the braid are all the same 18k gold tone. Do not redesign, restyle, resize or add anything. SCENE: the two cupped hands of an Indian woman of about sixty, held together in front of her, palms up, right hand slightly over the left, both thumbs lifted a little and pressed toward the camera as if about to hand the gift back, both thumbs visible: warm wheatish-brown skin, soft creases, fine knuckle lines, short unpainted nails, five fingers on each hand with correct anatomy; only the very tip of her right index finger carries the faintest pale haldi tint, far less saturated than the metal; every other fingertip is plain skin, no orange or yellow fingers; the faded indigo border of a soft cotton sari pallu falls across her left wrist; the hands absolutely bare: no bangles, no rings, no mehendi, no thread, no watch, no other jewellery. In the hollow of her palms lies the pair: one hoop flat on her palm showing the chevron plait, the other standing on its edge against her fingers, the disc and latch toward the camera. SCALE, the most important instruction: these are small, everyday 25 mm hoops and they must look small in her hands. Each hoop is only about one and a half of her fingertips wide, never two; the braid is narrower than one of her fingernails. The two hoops together, side by side, are narrower than one of her palms; skin shows on every side of each hoop, and the lying hoop covers only about one third of the width of the palm it rests in. Each hoop is about one sixth of the frame width, and the whole pair, disc and latch included, spans less than one third of the frame width. A dark, true contact shadow where each hoop touches skin. Never draw chunky statement hoops: the last two takes drew them about two and a third fingertips wide (about 35 mm), which is wrong. COMPOSITION: the pair sits high in her palms, near the heels of her hands: the top of the standing hoop's latch at about 40% down the frame and the lowest point of the lying hoop no lower than 52% down; the pair between 35% and 70% across. Both thumbs lift up off her hands and lean forward toward the camera as if to push the gift back, their tips between 38% and 48% down the frame, never above the hoops' top. The top 38% of the frame is calm dark cocoa wall only, with one faint warm glint of glass at the far top-right corner; no cabinet, vitrine, frame or counter. The left 22% of the frame is deep shadow: her right thumb there is only a dim shape with a thin rim of light. The light falls off fast below the hoops: below 58% down her curled fingers sink into deep shadow, her fingertips only dim warm shapes, and the bottom 30% is near-black lap and the indigo pallu, calm for a card. Last time the pair sat too low (half to two thirds down the frame), brightly lit fingers filled the lower frame and a lit thumb sat in the left shadow column; keep the pair high and everything below it dark. LIGHT: one bare warm tungsten bulb above left, soft, falling off fast into shadow; one small hard specular kicker from behind right draws a crisp pure-white highlight along every polished wire of the braid; a small neutral warm-white key falls on the hoops to keep their true colour, while the tungsten amber stays on the skin and the room. The warm pool is small and centred on the hoops and the middle of her palms; her fingers, thumbs and wrists fall off into shadow. GRADE: deep warm cocoa and umber, near-monochrome; the 18k gold tone is the only bright, saturated thing. The metal is the clean, bright lemon-yellow 18k gold tone of reference 1, with a pale butter-yellow disc and white mirror highlights; never orange, amber, copper, brassy or a deep 22k yellow. Natural film grain, believable imperfection, the hush of an Indian home at night. No face, no eyes, no eyebrows, no lips. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no printing on anything. One product only: this one pair of hoops; no other jewellery anywhere in the frame.
